Overview

Introduction

QTrans is a software package designed for calculating transport phenomena arising from quasiparticle scattering. It employs a finite-difference method to compute electron-quasiparticle coupling matrix elements, which are then used to determine properties such as electrical conductivity, resistivity, intrinsic breakdown strength, and superconducting critical temperature. QTrans supports input from both first-principles calculations and predicted Hamiltonians from machine learning methods such as HamGNN. These predictions can reduce the cost of obtaining electronic data for displaced supercells.

QTrans components

QTrans consists of two main components: preparation and calculation. Together, they provide a workflow from electronic-structure and phonon data to electron-phonon coupling and transport properties.

  • Preparation (QTrans_prep) converts electronic-structure outputs into the data format used by QTrans and constructs the real-space gradient matrices required for electron-phonon coupling calculations. It can use Hamiltonians obtained from first-principles calculations or machine learning predictions, and also provides tools for preparing phonon force-set data.

  • Calculation (QTrans_run) reads the prepared electronic, phonon, and coupling data to evaluate band structures, densities of states, electron-phonon matrix elements, and derived properties, including conductivity, carrier mobility, resistivity, intrinsic dielectric breakdown strength, and superconducting critical temperature.

The preparation step produces reusable datasets, allowing multiple calculations with different sampling meshes, temperatures, and other settings without repeating the underlying data preparation.

Software interfaces

The following software packages provide electronic data, Hamiltonian predictions, or phonon data used by QTrans. Available preparation interfaces depend on the workflow; consult the corresponding tutorial.

  • OpenMX (Open source package for Material eXplorer) is a software package for nanoscale material simulations based on density functional theory (DFT), norm-conserving pseudopotentials, and pseudo-atomic localized basis functions.

  • ABACUS (Atomic-orbital Based Ab-initio Computation at USTC) is an open-source computer code package based on density functional theory (DFT).

  • SIESTA is both a method and its computer program implementation, to perform efficient electronic structure calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of molecules and solids.

  • HONPAS (Hefei Order-N Packages for Ab initio Simulations) is an ab initio electronic structure calculation software package for linear scaling first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations of large-scale systems.

  • HamGNN is an E(3) equivariant graph neural network designed to train and predict ab initio tight-binding (TB) Hamiltonians for molecules and solids.

  • Phonopy is an open source package for phonon calculations at harmonic and quasi-harmonic levels.
